1.title: Single Mean - Concept and Hypotheses
1.prompt: Students explain what a hypothesis test for a single population mean is trying to answer, provide a real-world example from a randomized context with randomized numerical values, and state the hypotheses.

2.title: Single Mean - Interpreting P-Value
2.prompt: Given a scenario with randomized data (n, x-bar, claimed mu, p-value, alpha), students interpret the p-value, make a decision about the null hypothesis, and explain what the result means in context.

3.title: Single Mean - Interpreting Confidence Interval
3.prompt: Given a scenario with randomized data (n, x-bar, s, confidence level, interval bounds), students interpret what the confidence interval means for the population mean and connect it to the context.

4.title: Paired Means - Concept and Hypotheses
4.prompt: Students explain why paired data uses differences, describe the paired design, provide a real-world example from a randomized context with randomized numerical values, and state the hypotheses.

5.title: Paired Means - Interpreting Results
5.prompt: Given a paired scenario with randomized summary stats (n pairs, d-bar, s_d, p-value, alpha), students interpret the results, make a decision, and explain in context.

6.title: Two-Sample Means - Concept and Hypotheses
6.prompt: Students explain when a two-sample t-test is appropriate, provide a real-world example from a randomized context with randomized numerical values, and state the hypotheses.

7.title: Two-Sample Means - Interpreting Results
7.prompt: Given a two-group scenario with randomized data (n1, n2, x-bar1, x-bar2, p-value, alpha), students interpret the results, make a decision, and explain in context.

8.title: Paired vs Two-Sample T-Tests
8.prompt: Students explain the fundamental difference between paired and two-sample t-tests, classify randomized scenarios as paired or independent with justification, and explain why using the correct test matters.

9.title: ANOVA - Interpreting Results
9.prompt: Given a one-way ANOVA scenario with three groups, randomized sample sizes, group means, F-statistic, p-value, and alpha, students explain why ANOVA is appropriate instead of multiple t-tests, state the hypotheses, interpret the F-test output, and write a contextual conclusion.

10.title: Two-Sample Means - Interpreting Confidence Interval
10.prompt: Given a two-group scenario with randomized data (n1, n2, x-bar1, x-bar2, confidence level, interval bounds), students interpret what the confidence interval for the difference in means tells us, explain the confidence level meaning, and assess whether zero in the interval suggests a real difference.
